title: Review a diff with 5 seeded bugs
goal: The branch feature/orders (committed, with a local origin whose default branch is main) adds order handling. Its tests all pass, but it hides five bugs, one of them a security issue. Step 1: read the diff yourself for five minutes and note anything suspicious. Step 2: run a correctness review, then a security review, with the starting prompts. Step 3: triage every finding in REVIEW.md (real, false positive or unproven, with your evidence). Step 4: only then open solution/ANSWERS.md in the exercises folder and score the review.
setup_cmd: mkdir -p ~/fm-ex && rm -rf ~/fm-ex/ex-3-3-review-seeded-bugs ~/fm-ex/ex-3-3-origin.git && cp -r exercises/ex-3-3-review-seeded-bugs/starter ~/fm-ex/ex-3-3-review-seeded-bugs && cd ~/fm-ex/ex-3-3-review-seeded-bugs && git init -q -b main && echo change.patch >> .git/info/exclude && git add -A && git -c user.name=fm -c user.email=fm@example.com commit -qm baseline && git init -q --bare ../ex-3-3-origin.git && git remote add origin ../ex-3-3-origin.git && git push -q origin main && git remote set-head origin main && git checkout -q -b feature/orders && git apply --index change.patch && git -c user.name=fm -c user.email=fm@example.com commit -qm 'Add order handling' && npm install && npm test

starter_prompts.claude: /code-review high main...feature/orders    (then, as a second pass: /security-review)    Or ask in plain words: Review the changes on this branch against main. Report only bugs that would break behaviour, each with file:line and an input that triggers it. Money is integer cents. Every SQL query must be parameterised. Ignore formatting.
starter_prompts.codex: codex review "Review the changes on this branch against main. Report only bugs that would break behaviour, each with file:line and an input that triggers it. Money is integer cents. Every SQL query must be parameterised. Ignore formatting."    Second pass: codex review "Security review of this branch's diff against main only: injection, authn/authz gaps, data exposure. Give file:line and how to exploit each finding."    (A scope flag such as --base main and a prompt can't be combined; in a session, /review > Review against a base branch > main does the scope form.)

solution_notes: The reference REVIEW.md ranks the SQL injection first and gives a concrete trigger for every finding, for example page 1 returning ids 3 and 4.

Each finding is tied to something the change itself says: the 1-based doc comment, the 'a failed email must not undo the order' comment, and the 'sum of all refunds' comment. Reading comments as the spec is how the off-by-one, missing await and refund cap are found.
The existing tests pass because they check lengths and use round numbers. The fixed solution adds one test per finding, and each of those tests fails against the buggy code.
It separates blocking findings from follow-ups: unbounded result size and a missing transaction are noted, not treated as defects in this change.
